newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SELES CLINCHES FED CUP FOR UNITED STATES.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SELES CLINCHES FED CUP FOR UNITED STATES.

text.p: Co-world number one Monica Seles fought off a determined Arantxa Sanchez Vicario on Sunday to end the six-year U.S. Fed Cup title drought.
Seles battled Spain's great Fed Cup veteran for nearly two hours, claiming a 3-6 6-3 6-1 victory that gave the United States an insurmountable 3-0 lead in the best-of-five championship.
The victory ended Spain's domination of the women's team event and gave the United States its 15th Fed Cup title, but its first since 1990.
The Spanish team of Sanchez and Conchita Martinez was playing its sixth consecutive final and had won the Cup the last three years, beating the Americans in 1994 and 1995.
But Seles, who became an American citizen in 1994 and joined the U.S. team this year in the semifinals, altered the balance of power.
Seles easily beat Martinez in Saturday's opening singles and Olympic champion Lindsay Davenport downed Sanchez to give Seles a chance to clinch the tie early.
But Sanchez never goes down without a fight and the match with Seles was filled with big-hitting Grand Slam final calibre tennis.
When it was over, however, Seles had belted twice as many winner as Sanchez (42-19) and raised her career record against the fleet-footed Spaniard to 13-1.

"I was very nervous. I wasn't sure if I was going to be able to turn around but I hung in there," said Seles, who admitted to being far more nervous than she had ever been when playing just for herself -- even in the Grand Slams.
"All my teammates were behind me and I just hung in there," she said.
Said U.S. captain Billie Jean King: "I couldn't ask for a better team. They've been just fantastic, everyone just pulled together. "It's been a tremendous effort on everyone's part."
